THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
J.M.KHAZI J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, appellant who is the petitioner before the Tribunal is seeking enhancement of the compensation granted by the Tribunal for the injuries sustained by her in a motor vehicle accident dated 18.01.2020.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 18.01.2020, at 10.15 a.m., she was walking by the side of the road near Vidhya Rathna School, Deralakatte, Mangaluru Taluk.

Car bearing registration No.KA-19-MC- 9822 (for short 'offending vehicle'), driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came from Vidhya Rathna School side and proceeding towards Deralakatte, came in NC:
2024:KHC:20381-DB the extreme side of the road and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result of the accident, petitioner sustained permanent partial disability, affecting her earning capacity.
Before the accident, she was working as a tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Despite prolonged treatment, she is not completely cured.
As the owner of the offending vehicle, respondent is liable to pay the compensation and hence, the petition.
4. Despite due service of notice, respondent remained absent and as such placed ex-parte by the Tribunal.
5. In support of the petition, petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and 2 witnesses PW-2 and 3.

She relied upon Ex.P1 to 28.
6.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition and granted compensation in a sum of Rs.30,12,569/- together with NC: 2024:KHC:20381-DB interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent to pay the same.
7. Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, petitioner filed this appeal, contending that the Tribunal has erred in granting compensation under all the heads.
Though the disability is calculated at 80%, it has affected the earning capacity of the petitioner and therefore functional disability is required to be taken at 100%.
8. Before this Court also, respondent remained absent.

2 9.
We have heard learned counsel for petitioner and perused the record.
10. In the petition, the petitioner has given her age as 39 years.
Based on the passport at Ex.P24, the Tribunal has accepted her age as 39 years and therefore, the multiplier '15' taken is correct.

Though the petitioner has contended that she was doing tailoring and earning NC: 2024:KHC:20381-DB Rs.20,000/- p.m, no evidence is produced to establish the said fact and therefore, the Tribunal is justified in taking the income of the petitioner on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2020, based on minimum wages the notional income ought to have taken at Rs.14,000/-.

Anyhow,
the Tribunal has taken it at Rs.14,500/-.
Considering the evidence of PW-2 and 3, the Tribunal has accepted that the disability suffered by petitioner is 80% for whole body.

Based on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Co Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (Magma General Insurance)1, the Tribunal has rightly added 40% of the income towards loss of future prospects and calculated the compensation under the head loss of earning capacity as Rs.14,500x12x15x80% = Rs.20,88,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co Ltd Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (Magma General Insurance)1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, considering the nature of the injury suffered, at the rate of Rs.14,500/- for a period of 11 months, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,59,000/-.
Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.3,84,568.64 ps.
It also requires no interference.

Having regard to the nature of the injury suffered and disability sustained and also the fact that substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of earning capacity, the Tribunal is justified in granting compensation in a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head pain and suffering, Rs.1,00,000/- under the head loss of amenities of life, Rs.81,000/- under the head attendant, food, nourishment and conveyance charges and also Rs.50,000/- under the head future medical expenses.
The compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and there is no scope for interference by this Court.
In the result, the appeal fails and accordingly dismissed.
